extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring approximately 40K video frames (39,553 labeled frames) from video sequences across diverse indoor and outdoor environments under varied lighting conditions. Captured using a custom-built rig equipped with two 360° cameras in a vertical top-bottom setup paired with a synchronized LiDAR sensor, providing accurate depth and disparity labels via LiDAR point cloud projection onto equirectangular images, along with an augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built, remotely controlled robot chassis equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup (19.1 cm baseline) and an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor mounted 45.0 cm below the bottom camera, across indoor (corridors, halls) and outdoor (squares, parking, footpaths, roads) settings on a university campus under varied lighting and weather conditions. Device synchronization was managed via a hardware-triggered 33 ms flash visible in camera streams and timestamped in ROS.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw 4K/UHD equirectangular video streams (3840 x 1920 at 30 fps) from two Ricoh Theta V cameras and 64-beam LiDAR point clouds (at 10 fps) from an Ouster OS1-64 sensor mounted on a mobile robot.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: An automated depth completion pipeline tailored for 360° images was implemented to interpolate depth on spherical grid points. It aggregates point clouds across 9 temporal frames (m = 4 previous and 4 following scans), interpolates depth using k-nearest neighbors (k = 17) via inverse-distance weighted averaging, and applies relative variance uncertainty filtering (RIP = 0.8) and out-of-distribution thresholding (tOOD ≈ 0.37°) to remove uncertain or out-of-distribution points.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Matching LiDAR frame rate by retaining one of every three camera frames (down to 10 fps); aligning streams via flash marker; cropping unnecessary top and bottom regions (sky, ground); downsampling image width from 1024 to 512 (final resolution 1920x512 pixels); and filtering points outside the vertical field of view of the LiDAR.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Accurate ground-truth depth and disparity labels were generated automatically by optimizing rotation and translation matrices to project 3D LiDAR point clouds onto bottom equirectangular camera images using BFGS optimization on chessboard calibration points. Disparity values were mathematically derived from depth and camera baseline geometry.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment and projection accuracy was assessed by calculating Euclidean pixel error between LiDAR projections and image positions: averaging 1.7 pixels across 200 randomly selected points and 8.0 pixels across visually challenging areas (e.g., object edges) across sequences.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BFGS optimization algorithm, KISS-ICP (tested for odometry aggregation)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Occlusions were not explicitly handled; temporal point cloud aggregation is limited for fast-moving objects like cars; vertical field of view of ground truth is constrained to the LiDAR's 42.4° vertical coverage; collected within a single university campus; depth completion cannot ascertain exact object boundaries at depth edges.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and training stereo depth estimation and disparity estimation models, particularly omnidirectional (360°) stereo models for mobile robotics and dynamic human environments.
